headline: South Korea plans to spend 4.7 trillion won next year on a new frontier AI programme while insisting its existing national AI model project will go on.
score_reason: Lowered from 5: the briefing and the budget figures date from 2 Oct and 1 Sep, so the news is not new today.
importance_line: Shapes how Korean AI developers, from big firms to startups, will be funded, but the budget still needs parliament's approval and the selection rules are not yet set.
summary: The Asia Business Daily reports that the Ministry of Science and ICT will run a new Frontier AI project beside its "Dokpamo" independent foundation-model programme, after Vice Minister Ryoo Jaemyung said Dokpamo is "by no means being stopped" and will still pick two final teams after an evaluation in February. The 2027 budget proposal sets aside 4.7 trillion won, of which 3.9 trillion is for 10,000 "Vera Rubin" GPUs, with a detailed plan due after the National Assembly approves the budget in December.
notes: Briefing on 'the 2nd' (taken as 2 Oct, article dated 5 Oct); budget proposal from 1 Sep. Full article read.
